labels.label: schwdef:timelike_separated_set

hypotheses.paper: A, B, K ⊆ M; timelike curves σ : [0, 1] → M
hypotheses.note: ChronallySeparatedOn W K A B: every chronal curve of C or of C.dual of the open W over [0, 1] with σ 0 ∈ A, σ 1 ∈ B meets K; ChronallySeparated = On ⊤. Invariant under time reversal (dual_chronallySeparatedOn), symmetric in A, B (ChronallySeparatedOn.symm), monotone (ChronallySeparatedOn.mono: larger K, smaller A, B; Thm 4.11 Step 1.5 passes from K to U ⊇ closure K).
schw_def_2_14_iff (W = M) and chronallySeparatedOn_iff_of_isClosed (any open W); weakened in chronallySeparatedOn_iff_of_coe_eq: any open V with V = W ∖ K (K closed in W suffices).

hypotheses.paper: the reformulation: I^±(A, M ∖ K) are defined by timelike curves in M ∖ K (Def 2.2), which the 'clearly' uses
hypotheses.note: as causal arc-connectedness, for the ⇒ only: C.CausallyArcConnected (paper form), C.CausallyArcConnectedOn W (closed form), C.CausallyArcConnectedOn (W ∖ K) (general form). The ⇐ needs no hypothesis (chronallySeparatedOn_of_Iplus_Iminus: a curve avoiding K is a chronal curve of W ∖ K by CurveOn.restrict). The ⇒ fails without it: allRelated ℝ, K = {0}, A = {-1}, B = {1} (Causal.allRelated_chronallySeparated_not_iff). This is the target's `uses` (causally_arc_connected).

questions: Def 2.14 says 'timelike curve' with no direction. Reading taken: future or past directed (a chronal curve of C or of C.dual), which Sbierski's Defs 2.1–2.2 force in a time-oriented M (:235–241: one-sided tangents in one cone; 'future (past) directed … at some point (and hence at all points)'); with future curves only, the reformulation would lose its I⁻ clause. The reading is the paper's, recorded for the auditor, not an open question.

hypotheses.paper: M̃ a manifold, hence Hausdorff (standing assumption, InexSchwarzschild2.tex:228)
hypotheses.note: [T2Space M]; used (the limit of the curve at the exit parameter is unique) and needed: on the non-Hausdorff three-point Causal.ForkPoint with allRelated, a curve satisfying every other hypothesis is future-extensible through the other limit (Causal.forkPoint_leaving_futureExtensible). The separation-free core is futureInextensible_of_forall_not_tendsto.

hypotheses.note: an open embedding (IsOpenEmbedding ι), as in exists_leaving_of_isOpenEmbedding; only ι(N) open is used. not_continuousExtension_preimage (Sbierski's notion in N) asks ι continuous only.

hypotheses.paper: γ̃ a (future directed, after time reversal) timelike curve
hypotheses.note: futureInextensible_of_leaving takes a future CAUSAL curve of any open U ≥ W over [a, b]; the chronal form ChronalCurveOn.futureInextensible_of_leaving is the paper's. 'Otherwise reverse the time orientation' is D = C.dual; the C-only form is exists_leaving_inextensible_of_isOpenEmbedding (C.PastInextensible of the reversed curve over (-1, 0]).

hypotheses.paper: Lemma 2.17's hypotheses (connected M̃; the proof's 'Let q̃ ∈ I⁻(p̃, Ũ)')
hypotheses.note: exactly those of Causal.Causality.exists_leaving_of_isOpenEmbedding (Causal/LocateExtension.lean:418): [PreconnectedSpace M], [Nonempty N], range ι ≠ univ, C.CausallyArcConnected, HasChronalNeighbour at every frontier point (DEC-159's edge hypothesis, that lemma's, not new here).

questions: 'Future inextendible in M_Mink' (:485) read as ETT's FutureInextensible (DEC-11, DEC-13: no strict CAUSAL extension at the future end), stated in the open W = ι(N) of M̃ with C's relations at the opens of W (kb/0001; Rem 2.3), as the target's title says. Sbierski's own Def 2.10 (no CONTINUOUS extension to [a, b]) is proved too, in W (not_continuousExtension_of_tendsto) and in N for δ = ι⁻¹ ∘ γ (not_continuousExtension_preimage, the paper's literal sentence); it implies ETT's (futureInextensible_of_not_continuousExtension). ETT's notion in N needs a causality on N transported by ι (Rem 2.3, Causal.ChartIso): left to T-abs-c0-extension-skeleton.

kb_proposals: A causal curve of W over I with IsLUB I b, b ∉ I and no limit in W at b⁻ is future-inextensible in W, with no separation axiom and no time function: Causality.futureInextensible_of_forall_not_tendsto (CausalScaffold.SchwCausalLemmas); with T2, a curve of M over [a, b] in W on [a, b) leaving at b is: futureInextensible_of_leaving. Prefer them to InextensiblePiece's futureInextensible_of_isLUB_notMem (time function, I open, c continuous on ℝ) in the bounded case.

A cheap non-Hausdorff witness: Causal.ForkPoint (x generic, p and q in its closure and not separated, topology generateFrom {{x},{x,p},{x,q}}) with LineDevelopment.allRelated; toQ leaves {x,p} at 1 and is still future-extensible there through p (forkPoint_leaving_futureExtensible).

Sbierski's timelike separation (1507.00601 Def 2.14) is Causality.ChronallySeparatedOn W K A B (curves of C or C.dual over [0, 1]); its I^± reformulation for K closed is schw_def_2_14_iff, whose ⇒ needs causal arc-connectedness of W ∖ K (allRelated ℝ refutes it otherwise) and whose ⇐ needs nothing.
